system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s statements that the package is “FINAL”, market-standard or agreed at principal level do not evidence Buyer approval and do not override the playbook. In particular, no Amelia Frost approval has been given for either the 20% cap or 18-month period.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Starting position of **25% / AUD 6m**; 20% is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the draft. | **Counter at 25% / AUD 6m**—the proposed 20% fallback is presently unauthorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with liability only for the excess. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore the playbook thresholds**—the Seller’s proposal materially suppresses recovery through both inflated thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims; 18 months only with Amelia’s prior written approval, and no spillover into separate claim categories. | **Counter at 24 months and delete the all-Claims presumption**—the 18-month fallback is unauthorised and must not truncate separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject and insert the separate regime**—ownership, title and authority risks should not be treated as ordinary operational warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Make the comprehensive carve-out non-negotiable**—the playbook prohibits any waiver or contractual shelter for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed disclosure by data-room dump, public register or prudent search. | **Delete the general disclosures and require warranty-specific fair disclosure**—mere availability of material does not give the Buyer a fair understanding of an exception. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier must be tightly defined and not apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities, with Seller knowledge based on named persons and reasonable enquiry where relevant. | **Delete clause 8.3 as drafted**—it converts inadequate disclosure and constructive adviser knowledge into a broad release of Seller liability. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Effective Bluefen consent **and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Retain this as a strict Completion condition**—Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, so reasonable endeavours or bare delivery is inadequate. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion; any deferred release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval. | **Require repayment and releases through the Completion funds flow**—the Buyer should not acquire the company while Seller financing and security remain outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are treated as a Seller matter but omitted from the draft funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | Express Seller-funded line item covering **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**. | **Add the full liability to the funds flow or an equivalent specific Seller funding mechanism**—silence risks the acquired company bearing a Completion-triggered Seller obligation. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open, without independent verification or confirmatory assignment. | Broader protection for the Ironquay IP/ownership risk while preserving the contractual SOW3 payment cure; do not assume the AUD 180,000 figure is verified. | **Broaden the indemnity and require payment/assignment evidence**—a payment-only indemnity does not fully address ownership, transfer and resulting loss risks. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss amount. | Preserve relevant logs and evidence, require prompt investigation and continuing updates, and allocate remediation/cooperation appropriately without assuming breach, harm, notification duty or a numeric claim. | **Add preservation, investigation and update obligations while reserving liability**—the record is incomplete and supports neither dismissal nor a confirmed breach conclusion. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals, AUD 330,000 aggregate, characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction. | **Keep the item under diligence and reserve the price-mechanics position**—the disclosures do not establish either ordinary-course treatment or Debt classification. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded; Tax and IP are folded into the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, without a hidden general-regime override. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture with express category-specific precedence**—an “all Claims” formulation would defeat negotiated protections elsewhere. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence that the Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, title, encumbrance status, authority and valid transfer mechanics; DD-012 is only one supplied internal source. | **Require independent searches and Completion evidence rather than accepting DD-012 alone**—a company-maintained register is not independent proof of clean title or authority. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller asserts Tax and IP positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Treat both regimes as **open**, preserve category separation and make no assumption of unlimited liability or agreed resolution. | **Expressly mark Tax and IP as reserved for further negotiation**—the Seller cannot create agreement by characterising unresolved terms as settled. |
=== END ADVICE ===
